airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways and airport-related facilities.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land.
commercial: dense urban business area with organized building blocks and road access.
desert: broad barren area with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation.
farmland: regular cultivated land with visible parcel boundaries and agricultural texture.
footballfield: sports ground with a clear rectangular playing field and organized athletic layout.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with natural dark-green texture.
industrial: large factory-like compounds with utilitarian building layouts and heavy infrastructure.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with clear relief, slope variation, and irregular topographic texture.
park: planned green open space with vegetation, paths, and leisure-oriented organization.
parking: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout.
pond: small enclosed water body with compact water shape and clear boundary.
port: waterfront transport area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent infrastructure.
railwaystation: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures.
residential: housing area with repeated roof patterns and neighborhood street organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks.
viaduct: elongated elevated transport structure with clear grade-separated roadway form.
